We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl with a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline.

Structure: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) where substituent is /C=C/C(=O)N- phenyl-NH (aniline). So overall three disconnections: 1) sulfonamide formation between p-tolyl amine and sulfonyl chloride derived from sulfonyl chloride (maybe from p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride). 2) amide formation between α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid derivative) and aniline. 3) Doebner modification to form the α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde (maybe 4-formyl phenyl) and malonic acid.

Thus retrosynthetic steps: target -> disconnect amide bond: gives precursor A: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Wait amide bond is between C(=O) and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So cleavage gives acid: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Actually the acid side is the α,β-unsaturated acid: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2? Wait the amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the acid precursor is the α,β-unsaturated acid: /C=C/C(=O)OH attached to phenyl sulfonyl phenyl? Actually the acid is attached to the phenyl sulfonyl phenyl via the double bond: /C=C/ attached to phenyl sulfonyl phenyl? The SMILES: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl ring (c2) has substituent /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. So the acid precursor would be the same phenyl ring with /C=C/COOH (cinnamic acid) attached. So step 2: amide formation between cinnamic acid (attached to phenyl sulfonyl phenyl) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So precursor 2: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1 (the acid). Step 3: Doebner modification to form the α,β-unsaturated acid from aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid. So precursor 3: aldehyde phenyl sulfonyl phenyl: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2)cc1. Then sulfonamide formation: from p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride derived from sulfonyl chloride of phenyl sulfonyl? Actually sulfonamide formed between p-toluidine and sulfonyl chloride of phenyl sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph). So precursor 4: p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and phenyl sulfonyl chloride (ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2). So we need three reactions total, so combine steps: 1) Doebner to get aldehyde to unsaturated acid? Actually Doebner gives unsaturated acid directly from aldehyde + malonic acid. So step 1: Doebner: aldehyde + malonic acid -> unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid). So we need aldehyde precursor: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2)cc1. Step 2: amide coupling: unsaturated acid + aniline (c3ccccc3N) -> amide. Step 3: sulfonamide formation: p-toluidine + phenyl sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-CHO?) Wait the sulfonyl chloride must have the phenyl ring that later becomes the aldehyde. So we need phenyl sulfonyl chloride with aldehyde substituent: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2. So step 3: sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine and that sulfonyl chloride to give sulfonamide attached to aldehyde phenyl. That matches target after steps 1 and 2.

Thus final route: target -> disconnect amide -> unsaturated acid + aniline. Unsaturated acid from Doebner: aldehyde + malonic acid. Sulfonamide formation: p-toluidine + phenyl sulfonyl chloride (with aldehyde). So we need templates for these three reactions. We need to find template IDs for each. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria for each transformation.
